title: Adaptive gradient descent on Riemannian manifolds and its applications to Gaussian variational inference
claim: Our adaptive method converges faster and more stably than the standard baseline across step-size settings, shown on a representative problem.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, shared legend colors, log-scale left panel
description: Two line-plot panels side by side. The left panel, titled "Poisson regression GVI function value", plots F(μ_k) − F_min against iteration k on log-log axes. It shows three FBGVI baselines with different step settings (blue, green, purple), two RAdaGD variants (teal and red), and a flat olive Laplace Approximation line. The red RAdaGD curve drops fastest, by many orders of magnitude, and ends in numerical-noise jitter near 1e-13. The right panel, titled "Smallest eigenvalue tracking", plots λ_min(Σ_k) against iteration on a linear axis. All methods dip near 0.7 early and then settle at about 0.76. The green FBGVI curve instead stays near 1.04. The red curve shows early spikes. Legends are inside the plots, and the grid is light. The eye goes first to the steep red curve on the left.
caption: Comparison between FBGVI (Diao et al., 2023) and our methods on Poisson regression target π with ℓ= 50, n = 25. Left: F(µk) −Fmin, where Fmin is the minimum value among all experiments. Right: Minimum eigenvalues λmin(Σk) over the iteration.
abstract: We propose RAdaGD, a novel family of adaptive gradient descent methods on general Riemannian manifolds. RAdaGD adapts the step size parameter without line search, and includes instances that achieve a non-ergodic convergence guarantee, $f(x_k) - f(x_\star) \le \mathcal{O}(1/k)$, under local geodesic smoothness and generalized geodesic convexity. A core application of RAdaGD is Gaussian Variational Inference, where our method provides the first convergence guarantee in the absence of $L$-smoothness of the target log-density, under additional technical assumptions. We also investigate the empirical performance of RAdaGD in numerical simulations and demonstrate its competitiveness in comparison to existing algorithms.
